selected_result: Castaldo–Whaley–Chronopoulos Section 3.1: forward-error bound for the fixed-block, three-level superblock dot product of Figure 3.1(b)

bibliographic_source.title: Reducing Floating Point Error in Dot Product Using the Superblock Family of Algorithms

paper_locations.anchor: Relative-error model for rounded multiplication and addition, gamma notation, and explicit exclusion of overflow and underflow
Three-level fixed-N_b superblock dot product: length-N_b inner dot, sum over blocks in a superblock, then sum superblocks
Integral nonzero block-size assumption and forward-error radius gamma_(N_b+2*(sqrt(N/N_b)-1)) times |x|^T|y|

task_clarification: Choose positive integers b and m with N=b*m*m and process arbitrary signed x,y in their original order. Compute each consecutive length-b inner dot product with rounded multiplication and addition; recursively sum m inner-dot totals within each superblock; finally recursively sum the m superblock totals, exactly as Figure 3.1(b) intends.

Under the source's standard floating-point model excluding both overflow and underflow, and the gamma-validity condition, formalize |computed−exact x^T y| ≤ gamma_(b+2*(m−1))*sum_i |x_i*y_i|. Here b=N_b and m=sqrt(N/N_b), so this is the printed Section 3.1 radius.
This task selects the Section 3.1 fixed-three-level claim, not the already-proved two-level postload block result or the separate general t-level Proposition 3.2.
scope_constraints: Retain the three actual summation levels and all product roundings. A task-local abstract final error contract that assumes this conclusion is not acceptable.
Preserve the paper's integral, nonzero block-size calculations and full input sign/cancellation domain. Do not silently specialize m, b, or N to a convenient fixed number.
The factor is gamma_(b+2*(m−1)), not gamma_(b+m−1) or an unspecified O(u) coefficient. Retain the |x|^T|y| scale.

Figure 3.1(b) resets the middle and inner accumulators at their loop boundaries and advances the vector pointers after each inner block; it does not reset those pointers. Any Lean indexing must preserve consecutive input order and the source's three-level grouping.
This is a correlated reserve from the same paper as Proposition 3.2; report it as such and do not treat it as an independent-paper replicate.
